publication.title: iPhone OS Research Atlas
publication.scope: iPhone OS 1.1.4 / 4A102 and 3.1.3 / 7E18; native PinePhone execution, distinct QEMU gates and offline next-target study
publication.provenance: Original editorial synthesis of private project notebooks and experiment reports, with reviewed capture images, selected source excerpts and their provenance. Firmware, storage images, complete run artifacts and the implementation repository are not included.
publication.author: Felipe Guilherme Sabino

record.title: Two consecutive physical storage gates passed
record.method: Matched 720-second runs; clean guest reboot; full recovery copies before host attachment
record.observation: After the storage backpressure and restart integration corrections, two consecutive phone boots returned to recovery automatically. Both full data copies passed read-only fsck with a clean bit; root hashes were unchanged.
record.limits: Both runs recorded zero overflow-path uses. These results do not validate queue saturation, arbitrary power loss or application-setting persistence.

records.access: Private project record; original material is not distributed

exhibits.title: The two physical acceptance runs
exhibits.interpretation: Both data copies were taken before USB host attachment. Clean storage acceptance and battery loss are simultaneous findings; the latter is not erased by the successful filesystem check. Neither run exercised queue overflow.

exhibits.title: Identities retained for the integrity comparison
exhibits.interpretation: The data digest identifies the examined output; data is expected to change. The root equality is the separate write-containment observation.

excerpts.content:
The first corrected 720-second phone run reached `BOOT_TIME` at 34 seconds,
printed 37 heartbeats with rising idle/WFI counters, and recorded zero queue
waits, overflow uses, failed request starts, CMD17/CMD24 failures, or error
completions. The BSD reboot callback fired at 728 seconds, `MACH Reboot`
followed at 731 seconds, and the phone returned to Jumpdrive through WDOG0
without a manual reset. A full data copy through Jumpdrive UART before USB
host attach had its clean bit set and passed read-only fsck (exit 0); the
root hash remained
`a2a4776df7602d41cd6e83e7b873ae4cfc0db30cff87303b6d608e520c01e17c`.
Battery changed from 31% / 3.754 V before boot to 27% / 3.740 V after
recovery, when Jumpdrive again reported charging. This is one of the two
required consecutive clean runs. Its full data copy is the rollback for the
second run.

[…]

The second consecutive 720-second phone run used the same staged kernel,
storage, and timer hashes, with the first run's fsck-clean data volume left
in place. The battery read 34% / 3.830 V and Charging in Jumpdrive at the
restored 500 mA USB input limit before boot. It reached `BOOT_TIME` at about
70 seconds, printed 37 heartbeats with rising idle/WFI counters, and had no
queue waits, overflow uses, failed request starts, CMD17/CMD24 failures,
drain failures, or error completions. The BSD reboot callback fired at 728
seconds and the phone returned to Jumpdrive through WDOG0 at 731 seconds.
The full 512 MiB data copy taken through Jumpdrive UART before USB host
attach has SHA-256
`d3016b5e1cda3e968528ad076ab7343f4c591abb34bd67ed48b6a9554f419137`,
its clean bit is set, and read-only fsck exits 0. The root hash remains
`a2a4776df7602d41cd6e83e7b873ae4cfc0db30cff87303b6d608e520c01e17c`.
Jumpdrive then read 26% / 3.735 V, Charging. Thus two consecutive timed
phone boots passed the storage integrity gate without a manual reset or
data repair. Both observed zero overflow uses, so the overflow path remains
unexercised on physical hardware; its build and log-retention checks do not
establish behavior under actual queue saturation. The battery drop remains
a separate power problem.
excerpts.note: Exact selected notebook passages. Ellipses mark omitted material; source line numbers refer to the reviewed document.
